classification.reason: The reusable worldserver crashed before stop, identity closeout, cleanup, capture finalization, or immutable DVC publication. The wrapper therefore had no admissible acceptance_source_report.json to audit and no batch whose stored result could be trusted.

crash_localization.apport_reason: The locally built executable did not belong to a package, so apport discarded the core.
crash_localization.journal_signal: Each Azil phase-two shard wave logged MoveSplineInitArgs::_checkPathLengths failures for NPC entry 42355. The final wave preceded the SIGSEGV.
crash_localization.invalid_spline_cause: npc_azil_seismic_shard::FillPath appended the elevated endpoint twice, creating a zero-length final segment rejected by MoveSplineInitArgs::_checkPathLengths.
crash_localization.unsafe_iterator_cause: npc_azil_seismic_shard dereferenced Vehicle::GetNextEmptySeat(0, false) without checking Seats.end(). Vehicle::GetNextEmptySeat explicitly returns Seats.end() when every usable seat is occupied or has a pending join.
crash_localization.long_fight_trigger: The route reached repeated seismic-shard cycles during the long Azil encounter, exposing the otherwise latent full-or-pending-full vehicle path.
evidence: Generation 1 terminalized and the run reached 13/14 terminals, so the rerun179 shared passive-swarm staging correction resolved the rerun178 deadlock.
The crash occurred only after generation 14 began and the journal repeatedly identified seismic-shard entry 42355.
No bot, role-audit, route-gate, or watchdog result can be inferred after the server process disappeared.

bounded_correction.behavior: Remove the duplicate terminal spline point. Preserve the existing reverse seat preference, but compare the returned iterator with vehicle->Seats.end() before dereference; despawn only the orphan shard when no usable or non-pending seat exists.
unchanged_contracts: all Phase 9 role and route thresholds
all bot spell, threat, movement, hazard, Misdirection, healer-handoff, and passive-staging behavior
Azil health, damage, phase timing, shard count, target selection, and occupied-seat behavior
identity, exact party, serial isolation, publication, cleanup, hydration, and targeted-eviction contracts
